narrative:
The model estimated that you have a 35% probability of being a bad credit risk. That is a meaningful risk level and it falls above the bank’s acceptance threshold, which is why the application was denied.

The most influential factor was your checking-account status. Because no checking-account information was recorded—a situation shared by most approved applicants—this factor actually counted in your favour and reduced the risk estimate. The second most important factor was the amount requested. You asked for 10,366 DM, far above the approved-applicant average of about 3,020 DM, and this strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit. The third most important factor was the repayment duration. A 60-month term is much longer than the approved average of about 19 months, and this also increased the perceived risk. Although your checking-account status helped, the unusually large amount and long repayment period outweighed it and led to denial.

To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller loan and a shorter repayment period, which would reduce both the amount at risk and the time over which repayment could go wrong. It would also help to discuss your application with the bank, provide stronger evidence of savings or account history, and reapply once the requested amount and term are closer to what the bank typically accepts.
